set_title: Vasculitis: vessel size, lungs and serology
stem: A 51-year-old man has 2 months of chronic sinus congestion, cough and low-grade fever. Chest imaging shows patchy opacities in both lungs. Leukocyte count is 9,000/mm3 with 28% eosinophils, and ANCA is positive. Biopsy of the nasal mucosa shows necrotizing vasculitis of small vessels with granulomas.
oneliner: 51M + sinus congestion + cough + patchy lung opacities + eosinophils 28% + ANCA positive + granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: PAN **spares the lungs** and is ANCA-negative; he has lung opacities and a positive ANCA
whyNot.C: GPA does not cause **marked eosinophilia**; his eosinophils are 28% of 9,000/mm3
whyNot.D: IgA vasculitis is **palpable purpura with IgA deposits**, mainly in children, and does not form granulomas
whyNot.E: Cryoglobulinemia is an **immune-complex** vasculitis with purpura and low C4; it does not form granulomas or involve the sinuses

why: Same man, one change: **eosinophils 28% instead of 2%** (about 2,500/mm3). Sinus disease, lung opacities and a granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis with **marked eosinophilia** is EGPA; ask about adult-onset asthma, which nearly all patients have.

head: Vessel size
Lungs involved
Serology
Hallmark
rows: Segmental transmural necrosis of different ages; microaneurysms; hypertension, neuropathy, bowel ischemia
**Palpable purpura on buttocks and legs**, abdominal pain, arthritis, hematuria
**Cryoglobulins, rheumatoid factor, low C4**; hepatitis C

idea.rule: Granulomatous vasculitis of sinuses and lungs: marked eosinophilia (with asthma) = EGPA; normal eosinophils = GPA.
also: EGPA was formerly called Churg-Strauss syndrome
Asthma and nasal polyps usually come years before the vasculitis
p-ANCA (MPO) is positive in about 40%; mononeuritis multiplex is common
